category.name: Untrusted Input Handling and Buffer Overflow

rule.name: Unsafe String Manipulation: strcpy(), strcat(), sprintf(), etc.
rule.rule_desc: Application data is inserted into an HTML or script rendering context, or marked safe in a way that may bypass automatic encoding.
rule.vuln_desc: If attacker-controlled content reaches an executable browser context, it may run under the application’s origin, read accessible session data, or perform actions with the victim’s permissions.
rule.developer: Use automatic context-aware output encoding and data-only DOM APIs. Sanitize deliberately accepted rich HTML with a maintained allowlist sanitizer and avoid marking untrusted content as safe.
rule.reviewer: Identify instances of these functions and validate that safer alternatives are used with proper size limits. This can be confirmed as an issue when the matched path is reachable and required controls are missing, weak, or inconsistent.

rule.name: Potential Buffer Overflow: strncpy() Misuse
rule.rule_desc: The code uses a low-level memory, formatting, allocation, or type-conversion operation whose safety depends on bounds, types, initialization, and caller invariants.
rule.vuln_desc: A violated memory or formatting invariant may expose process memory, corrupt application state, crash the process, or permit code execution when an attacker can influence the relevant inputs.
rule.developer: Validate sizes and types before use, use bounded and type-safe APIs, and keep format strings fixed. Prefer checked conversions and safe ownership abstractions; document and test every remaining unsafe invariant.
rule.reviewer: Confirm proper use of `strncpy()` and size calculations to avoid off-by-one errors. This can be confirmed as an issue when the matched path is reachable and required controls are missing, weak, or inconsistent.

rule.name: Unbounded Memory Allocation
rule.rule_desc: The code manages allocation, ownership, indexed access, or resource release. Confirm capacity, lifetime, nullability, and transfer of ownership across callers.
rule.vuln_desc: An invalid lifetime or out-of-range access may corrupt memory, disclose process data, or crash the application. Unbounded or unreleased resources may exhaust memory and deny service under repeated use.
rule.developer: Enforce bounds and lifetime invariants, handle allocation failure, and use appropriate automatic resource ownership. Confirm a leak or invalid access before adding cleanup that could introduce double release.
rule.reviewer: Ensure that memory allocations based on user input are properly constrained. This can be confirmed as an issue when the matched path is reachable and required controls are missing, weak, or inconsistent.

rule.name: Unsafe Execution Functions: system(), exec(), etc.
rule.rule_desc: The code invokes a process or shell execution API. Trace the executable, arguments, shell use, and source of externally supplied values.
rule.vuln_desc: If attacker-controlled data changes command syntax or executable selection, an attacker may execute commands with application privileges, read or modify files, or disrupt service.
rule.developer: Use a fixed executable with a separate argument array and avoid a shell where possible. Validate arguments for the selected program and allowlist permitted operations.
rule.reviewer: Identify all instances of execution functions. Verify that input is properly sanitized and ensure only trusted data is used. This can be confirmed as an issue when the matched path is reachable and required controls are missing, weak, or inconsistent.

rule.name: Use of `system()` with Hardcoded Paths
rule.rule_desc: The checked source or build configuration embeds potentially sensitive credential or key material. Determine whether it is active and whether it reaches distributed artifacts or logs.
rule.vuln_desc: A party who can read exposed source, artifacts, configuration, or logs may recover active secrets and access the protected service or decrypt data with the secret owner’s privileges.
rule.developer: Remove active secrets from source and build layers, rotate exposed values, and load replacements through a restricted secret-management facility. Use narrowly privileged, short-lived credentials.
rule.reviewer: Confirm that no dangerous paths are used in `system()` calls. This can be confirmed as an issue when the matched path is reachable and required controls are missing, weak, or inconsistent.

rule.name: Temporary Files: Use of mkstemp()
rule.rule_desc: The code accesses, creates, deletes, or shares filesystem data. Resolve path provenance, destination containment, permission modes, and any concurrent access.
rule.vuln_desc: An attacker controlling a path or shared file may read or replace private files, delete data, or redirect an operation outside its intended directory if containment and access controls are ineffective.
rule.developer: Resolve paths beneath a fixed permitted root and verify containment and effective permissions. Use safe exclusive temporary-file creation, restrict sharing, and account for symlinks and concurrent changes.
rule.reviewer: Check for any usage of `mktemp()` and suggest replacements with `mkstemp()`. This can be confirmed as an issue when the matched path is reachable and required controls are missing, weak, or inconsistent.

rule.name: Insecure File Permissions
rule.rule_desc: The code or deployment configuration requests privileges or grants access beyond an explicitly resolved minimum. Determine the effective permissions and the operation’s requirements.
rule.vuln_desc: A compromised actor may access additional data, modify protected resources, or extend compromise beyond the intended application boundary when excessive privileges remain available.
rule.developer: Run with the least privileges required, remove unnecessary grants, and scope each permission to its intended resource and operation. Verify effective inherited permissions and test denied access.
rule.reviewer: Verify that file creation follows proper permission practices, especially in privileged code. This can be confirmed as an issue when the matched path is reachable and required controls are missing, weak, or inconsistent.

rule.name: Unsafe Use of Process Environment Variables
rule.rule_desc: The code declares an entry point, model, destination, or configuration value that may cross a trust boundary. Identify callers, recipients, and the required data-access policy.
rule.vuln_desc: A boundary that trusts unauthorized callers or exposes private output may permit data disclosure or state changes. A declaration, address, or architectural marker alone does not establish such a failure.
rule.developer: Trace the actual boundary, restrict accepted inputs and recipients, and enforce authentication and object-level authorization where required. Verify both authorized and denied use cases.
rule.reviewer: Verify that sensitive data is not passed via the environment. If unavoidable, restrict access to the process environment properly. This can be confirmed as an issue when the matched path is reachable and required controls are missing, weak, or inconsistent.

rule.developer: Run with the least privileges required, remove unnecessary grants, and scope each permission to its intended resource and operation. Verify effective inherited permissions and test denied access.
rule.reviewer: Confirm that all privilege-dropping operations are performed securely and in the correct sequence with proper error handling. This can be confirmed as an issue when the matched path is reachable and required controls are missing, weak, or inconsistent.

rule.name: Improper Use of `memset` for Sensitive Data
rule.rule_desc: The code handles private data or configures build and process hardening. Determine which information is retained and what protection the deployed artifact actually supplies.
rule.vuln_desc: Insufficient memory, diagnostic, or build protections may make private values easier to recover or increase the consequences of another defect. Their absence alone does not establish an exploit path.
rule.developer: Minimize private data lifetimes and diagnostic exposure, apply the platform’s appropriate hardening controls, and verify the final binary rather than inferring protection from source markers alone.
rule.reviewer: Check if the data cleared using `memset` is sensitive (passwords, keys, etc.) and confirm if a secure clearing method (like `explicit_bzero`) is implemented to prevent compiler optimizations. This can be confirmed as an issue when the matched path is reachable and required controls are missing, weak, or inconsistent.
